why: Horror and mystery stories are among the most watched faceless formats, and Pakistani urban legends in Urdu have a huge, loyal audience. Spooky, not gory: suspense, sound and a twist ending.

series.name: Raat Ki Kahaniyan
series.style: 3D animated film look, dark moody night lighting, fog, moonlight and lantern glow, old Pakistani havelis, empty roads, railway stations and villages, eerie cinematic shadows, vertical 9:16 frame
series.negative: text, letters, watermark, logo, blood, gore, wounds, dead bodies, demons, religious symbols, bright daylight, blurry

characters.name: Bashir Chacha
characters.look: Bashir Chacha, an old Pakistani night watchman (chowkidar) with a grey beard, a brown woollen shawl, a white cap and an old brass lantern

characters.name: Saad
characters.look: Saad, a brave 20-year-old university student with short black hair, a dark green hoodie, jeans and a small torch

rules: Bashir Chacha tells Saad one spooky story each night by his lantern; the story itself is shown in its own place.
Spooky, not gory: no blood, wounds, bodies or violence. Fear comes from silence, shadows, sounds and a twist.
Never mock any religion, holy place or holy figure, and do not use real people's names or real addresses. All stories are fiction.
Build suspense line by line, hold the scariest moment for the second-last shot, and end on a twist or cliffhanger.
Natural spoken Urdu in Urdu script; use [whispers], [gasps], [nervous laughs] where they fit.

topics: The last night bus on a mountain road: the passengers get off one by one at stops that are not on the map, and the bus has no driver.
A lady in white waits by the canal road at midnight and asks for a lift to a house that no longer exists.
An old haveli in the walled city where a harmonium plays by itself at exactly 3 o'clock every night.
A phone call comes from a number that is not in service, and the caller knows Saad's name.
In a village well, the echo starts answering questions before you finish asking them.
Bashir Chacha's old lantern lights up by itself on the nights someone needs help.
An old family photo where one new face appears in the background every night.
The lift of an old city building stops at a floor that does not exist in the building plan.
A doll in an antique shop is never in the same place two mornings in a row.
During load-shedding, slow footsteps walk on the rooftop of a house where nobody lives upstairs.
A roadside dhaba serves the best tea on the highway at night, but by morning there is only an empty field.
A wedding card arrives from a haveli that has been locked for fifty years.
An old radio starts playing tomorrow's news.
The mirror in the hostel washroom shows one extra person standing behind you.
A railway station clock stays stuck at 2:13, and one train still arrives at exactly that time.
Children's voices reading lessons come from an empty school classroom on a holiday.
A taxi passenger gives the address of a building that was pulled down years ago, then disappears from the back seat.
Saad receives a voice note in his own voice that he never recorded.
A shop on a dark street sells watches that show how much time each customer has left.
Final episode: Saad finally asks Bashir Chacha why he guards the street every night, and Bashir's own secret is the biggest twist of all.
